title: The insurer's library before go-live
scenario:
You are a project lead at a travel insurer. The call centre wants an assistant that answers agents' questions about policies, claims and prices. The plan is to load the company's documents into a hosted vector store next week.

You run a data readiness check first. The exhibit shows your inventory and one test chunk.
exhibit:
Knowledge base inventory (made-up example data)

Source              Format  Size       Copies                Updated   Owner
A Policy wordings   PDF     1,200 pp   3 versions            2025-04   Legal
                                       (2023, 2024, 2025)
B Claims FAQ        wiki    90 pp      1                     2026-09   Claims
C Price tables      .xlsx   40 sheets  1                     2026-09   Pricing
D Old intranet      .html   300 pp     unknown               2019      nobody

Test chunk from source A (default chunking):
  "Medical cover: 2,000,000 EUR. Excess: 150 EUR. Cover ends
   on the date of return."
  (The country and plan name appear only in the page heading.)

Test set: none yet

questions.prompt: Source A has three versions. What should go into the knowledge base?

options.text: All three versions, so the assistant can compare how the wording changed over time.
options.explanation: Agents need today's wording. Old versions compete with it, and OpenAI's accuracy guide warns that irrelevant context drowns out the real information.

options.text: All three versions, plus a line in the prompt that says "prefer the newest version".
options.explanation: The search may return only old chunks for a question, and the model may not know which version they come from.

options.text: Only the 2025 version; archive the 2023 and 2024 copies outside the knowledge base.
options.explanation: Right. One current version removes the noise. OpenAI's retrieval guide also shows filters for files you can't remove.

options.text: None of the versions, because policy wordings are too long to be split into chunks.
options.explanation: Long documents are what chunking is for. OpenAI's guide accepts files up to 5,000,000 tokens.

questions.prompt: What should the team do with source C, the price tables in .xlsx?

options.text: Load them as they are, because the vector store converts every spreadsheet automatically on upload.
options.explanation: On 2026-10-06, OpenAI's retrieval guide did not list .xlsx as a supported file type. Check the list; don't assume.

options.text: .xlsx is not on OpenAI's list (2026-10-06): convert, check the result, or use another route.
options.explanation: Right. The supported list includes formats such as .pdf, .docx and .txt, but not .xlsx. Convert the tables and check them, or answer price questions another way.

options.text: Paste a screenshot of each sheet into the policy PDF so it is indexed with the wording.
options.explanation: That mixes prices into a different document and hides the numbers in images. It makes the data harder to keep current and to check.

options.text: Leave prices out of the project for good, since retrieval can't work with numbers.
options.explanation: Retrieval can work with numbers in supported text. The problem here is the file format, not the numbers.

questions.prompt: Look at the test chunk. What is the best fix?

options.text: Make each chunk as small as possible, so that every chunk holds exactly one number.
options.explanation: A smaller chunk still lacks the country and plan. It would lose even more meaning.

options.text: Turn off chunk overlap, so the page headings are not repeated across chunks.
options.explanation: Overlap is not the problem. The heading text is missing from the chunk, so removing overlap can't add it back.

options.text: Ask agents to always say the country first, so the model can guess the right plan.
options.explanation: The chunk itself still doesn't say which plan it belongs to. The model would be guessing between plans.

options.text: Add short context to each chunk, such as the country and plan from the page heading.
options.explanation: Right. This is the fix in Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval post: add chunk-specific context before indexing.

questions.prompt: What is the most important thing missing before the go-live next week?

options.text: A test set: 20 or more real agent questions with the right answer and its source.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's accuracy guide calls an evaluation set of 20+ questions with ground-truth answers the right baseline. The inventory says "none yet".

options.text: Source D loaded as well, so the assistant has the widest possible coverage.
options.explanation: Source D is from 2019, has unknown copies and no owner. Loading it adds old, unowned content that may conflict with current policy.

options.text: A larger model, chosen before any testing, so quality is high from the first day.
options.explanation: Without a test set, you can't tell whether a larger model helps. Measure first, then choose.

options.text: A target that the assistant gives zero wrong answers in its first month of use.
options.explanation: That target is not realistic. OpenAI's accuracy guide says models are unlikely to reach 99.999% accuracy with off-the-shelf methods; set a measured target instead.
